So.

My background is actually media and marketing.

I had my own company which I sold in 2016 and during that process I realized that there wasn't a lot for creative founders out there, particularly, particularly M A advisors that work anywhere in, in the sort of media sphere, they tend to still be very much sort of accountants and lawyers that came out of the media industry.

After I sold my business, one of my friends who's CEO of a listed company in the UK actually approached me and said, look, we're looking to buy other agencies that are similar to your company that you just sold, so can you help us?

So it quickly grew.

So I haven't really done it on my own because I'm used to running as an entrepreneur.

We got locked down, which was fantastic, because as somebody had built a digital business before, it just opened up the whole of America immediately, which we went straight after and have never looked back, really.
So the business built very quickly in the US we no longer needed to be present in anybody's office.
That's when I moved to Tulum, when clients understood that I could be a call away and I didn't have to be in the office.
Yeah.

And as you can imagine, Carolina, you know, we are obviously speaking across the Atlantic right now, but prior to that, the trust really was required for you to go and sit in somebody's office for an hour or so.
The business has blown up for us since then.
So the last five years has been very much international transactions, and they've involved businesses in Germany, Belgium, Turkey, Israel, and lots in America and the UK as well.
So.
So it's.
It is very much an international business.
We haven't done anything in South America yet, but we have worked with.
A.
Few Mexican expats that are based in the US now.
So they.

So, yeah, that.
That's what I was gonna ask because I'm.

Colombia is very, very little.

And then they.
They disappeared.

They paid everything to us.

I invoice mostly in Mexico and Chile.

But it wasn't tax.

That's why I ended up having each company in each country.
Yeah.

Yeah, that that is holding all of the shares in all of the businesses.

So.

summary.overview:
- Capital A Company has 7 years of M&A advisory experience, focusing primarily on US transactions and managing approximately 30 active clients across 13 agency deals.
- Andy Day founded Capital A after identifying a gap in M&A services for creative founders following his media business sale in 2016.
- Carolina operates companies in Mexico, Chile, and Colombia, with primary revenue from Mexico and Chile, and is celebrating a 10-year anniversary this year.
- The M&A process begins with a 45-minute onboarding meeting, followed by tasks such as tax return requests and marketing material creation, with ongoing client input.
- Valuation involves three methods, and the target list for potential buyers will focus on interest in the Mexican and Chilean markets.
- The overall timeline for the M&A process spans 4-5 months, with offers anticipated by the end of month 4.
- Carolina has a scheduling conflict due to Mexico City meetings during July 7-11 but can accommodate changes around this period.
- Carolina plans to disclose her pregnancy early in the process to mitigate complications post-offer, with maternity leave expected to start around November 15th.
- Capital A's pricing structure was adjusted to $5,000 monthly payments over 6 months, addressing Carolina's cash flow concerns.
summary.short_summary: Capital A Company, founded by Andy Day to fill a gap in M&A services for creative founders, boasts 7 years of advisory experience, primarily in US transactions and serving around 30 active clients through 13 agency deals. Carolina, who operates businesses in Mexico, Chile, and Colombia, is celebrating her 10-year anniversary and aims to discuss the M&A process, which starts with a 45-minute onboarding meeting followed by necessary tasks. The valuation will employ three methods, with a target list focusing on the Mexican and Chilean markets, and the entire process is expected to span 4-5 months. Carolina mentioned a scheduling conflict from July 7-11 but is flexible, and she plans to disclose her pregnancy early to manage her maternity leave starting around November 15. Capital A adjusted its pricing to $5,000 monthly over six months to accommodate Carolina's cash flow concerns.
